items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the Hudson river park act, in relation to development or
redevelopment of Pier 40 in the Hudson river park
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6565

SPONSOR: KAVANAGH
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the Hudson river park act, in relation
to development or redevelopment of Pier 40 in the Hudson river park

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to allow for the redevelopment of Pier 40 in
the Hudson River Park, with a wider range of potential uses than are
currently permitted.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill amends paragraph (b) of subdivision 9 of the
Hudson River Park Act, to permit development or redevelopment of Pier 40
to include business, professional, or governmental office space, not to
700,000 square feet, with up to 100,000 square feet for offices and
operations of the Hudson River Park Trust (the "Trust"). The maximum
height of any building would be 88 feet, including any space for mechan-
ical features of the building, and any development or redevelopment
would require at least 320,000 square feet of playing field space and a
minimum footprint of 65% of the pier devoted to passive and active
public open space. The Trust would also be required to establishes a
Pier 40 Task Force to review any request for proposals, and any develop-
ment or redevelopment would be subject New York City's Uniform Land Use
Review Procedure.

Section two of the bill amends Subdivision 11 of the Hudson River Park
Act, to allow the Trust to enter into a 49 year lease on Pier 40, with a
25 year renewal and an additional 24 year renewal.

Section three of the bill amends Paragraph (vi) of Subdivision (g) of
the Hudson River Park Act, to allow business, professional, or govern-
mental offices on Pier 40.

Section four of the bill sets forth the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION

In 1998, the Hudson River Park Act was enacted, creating the Hudson
River Park with a legal obligation that commercial nodes within the park
generate income to help fund operations and maintenance. The largest of
those commercial nodes, Pier 40, has a mix of allowable uses but does
not allow commercial office space. In the intervening decades, Pier 40
has been heavily used for active sports, recreational human-powered
boating, commercial maritime uses, office space for the Trust, and park-
ing for the local community. Despite significant capital investment from
the City, State, and Federal governments, the Trust will needs addi-
tional funding; which development or redevelopment of Pier 40 would
potentially provide. The commercial office space that would be permitted
by this bill may facilitate development that would help the Trust meet
its obligations for Hudson River Park.

The amendment to the Act establishes limitations on any development or
redevelopment of Pier 40 that are intended to balance the need for addi-
tional revenue, community concerns about the scale of any new buildings,
and the continuing need for passive and active recreational spaces.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

Minimal.


 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Relates to development or redevelopment of Pier 40 in the Hudson river park and amount of passive and active public open space necessary for such development or redevelopment.
